description: Remote-mode escape-safe segmentation for `cmux send`. cmux send turns the two-character sequences backslash-n, backslash-r and backslash-t into Enter, Enter and Tab, so a prompt that contains them as text (a regex, a code snippet, a Windows path) would submit itself half-typed. A backslash that is not followed by n/r/t within the same send is delivered literally, so the text is split right after every backslash that precedes n, r or t, and each segment is sent with its own `cmux send -- <segment>`. Line breaks are flattened first (see line-breaks.json). Splitting is per user-perceived character (Swift Character / extended grapheme cluster), so surrogate pairs, emoji sequences and CJK text are never cut. At most 12 splits are made (13 segments); escapes past the cap are left to cmux rather than spawning hundreds of subprocesses. Segments always concatenate back to the flattened input and are never empty.
function: RemoteControlService.escapeSafeSegments(_:) — input string in, ordered list of segments out (empty input gives an empty list)
verifiedBy: Characterization of the Swift implementation (spec #93, ticket #120); Tests/PowerUpTests/TextSafetyFixtureTests.swift. The cmux escaping rule it defends against (backslash + n/r/t is interpreted, a backslash ending a send is literal) was verified live against the cmux CLI at /Applications/cmux.app/Contents/Resources/bin/cmux when remote mode was built (DESIGN.md remote-control addendum, 2026-08-25); the cmux version was not recorded at the time.

cases.name: empty input sends nothing
cases.reason: Empty text must produce zero cmux send calls, not one empty send.

cases.name: plain text is one segment
cases.reason: Ordinary dictation (the overwhelming majority) must cost exactly one cmux send.

cases.name: backslash-n in a regex is defused
cases.reason: cmux would turn backslash-n into Enter and submit 'match ' half-typed; ending the send after the backslash keeps it literal.

cases.name: backslash-r is defused
cases.reason: backslash-r is also Enter to cmux and would submit early.

cases.name: backslash-t is defused
cases.reason: backslash-t is Tab to cmux, which in Claude Code's prompt triggers completion instead of typing the text.

cases.name: escape at the very start
cases.reason: An escape in column 0 is split after the lone backslash; the first send is just the backslash.

cases.name: escape at the very end
cases.reason: A trailing backslash-n must not become a premature submit before the explicit Enter.

cases.name: only an escape gives two non-empty segments
cases.reason: A split never produces an empty segment (an empty cmux send).

cases.name: lone trailing backslash is not split
cases.reason: A backslash with nothing after it is already literal; splitting would add a pointless send.

cases.name: backslash before other letters is not split
cases.reason: Only n, r and t follow-ups are cmux escapes; other backslashes are delivered literally in one send.

cases.name: Windows path with backslash-n and backslash-t
cases.reason: A dictated Windows path would otherwise press Enter at \new and Tab at \temp.

cases.name: uppercase N, R, T are not escapes
cases.reason: The split is case-sensitive: only the lowercase sequences are cmux escapes, so these stay one send.

cases.name: run of different escapes
cases.reason: Back-to-back escapes are each defused; every backslash ends its own send.

cases.name: run of repeated backslash-n
cases.reason: A double escaped newline in a code snippet must not submit twice.

cases.name: double backslash before n
cases.reason: Only the backslash directly before n pairs with it; the split goes after the second backslash so no send ends in backslash-n.

cases.name: real LF is flattened before splitting
cases.reason: A raw LF handed to cmux send is Enter just like backslash-n; segmentation must be safe even if the caller forgot to flatten.

cases.name: backslash before a real newline is not fused with the next n
cases.reason: Flattening turns the newline into a space first, so the backslash is no longer adjacent to the n and stays literal.

cases.name: backslash before a real tab character
cases.reason: A real tab character is not the letter t, so it does not form a cmux escape with the backslash.

cases.name: shell metacharacters are one segment
cases.reason: cmux is spawned with an argument vector, not a shell, so quotes, dollars and backticks must arrive unchanged in a single send.

cases.name: leading dashes are one segment
cases.reason: Dash-leading text is protected by the `--` separator, not by splitting; segmentation must leave it whole.

cases.name: surrogate pairs around an escape
cases.reason: Astral-plane emoji are UTF-16 surrogate pairs; the split must fall between characters, never inside a pair.

cases.name: ZWJ sequence and flag stay whole
cases.reason: Multi-scalar emoji (zero-width-joiner sequences, regional-indicator flags) must not be cut by a split.

cases.name: CJK text around an escape
cases.reason: Chinese dictation containing a literal backslash-n is split only at the backslash, with every CJK character intact.

cases.name: CJK, kana and hangul without escapes are one segment
cases.input: 你好，世界。日本語のテキスト、한국어 텍스트
expected: 你好，世界。日本語のテキスト、한국어 텍스트
cases.reason: Non-Latin text with full-width punctuation contains no cmux escapes and must cost exactly one send.

cases.name: full-width backslash and yen sign are not escapes
cases.reason: Only the ASCII backslash U+005C starts a cmux escape; look-alikes common in CJK input are left alone.

cases.name: line breaks only become a single space segment
cases.reason: Break-only input flattens to one space and is sent as one non-empty segment, never as Enter.

cases.name: twelve escapes are all defused
cases.reason: Up to the cap of 12 splits every escape is defused, giving 13 sends.

cases.name: thirteenth escape is past the segment cap
cases.reason: Pathological input must not spawn hundreds of cmux processes: after 12 splits the remainder goes in one last send and cmux's interpretation is accepted (deliberate trade-off).

cases.name: a combining mark on the backslash is not an escape
cases.reason: Splitting compares whole characters: a backslash that a combining mark extends is another character, so no split is made (cmux sees the mark, not n, after the backslash).

cases.name: a combining mark on the n means no split
cases.reason: Characters are compared whole, so n with a combining mark is not the letter n and the text stays one send. Recorded as Swift does it: cmux may still read the backslash-n bytes, and every implementation must agree on this edge.

cases.name: a prepended scalar joins the backslash
cases.reason: A Prepend scalar (U+0600) makes one character with the backslash that follows it, so that backslash is not a lone backslash and nothing is split; the cluster rules must match Swift's.
